ORIENTATION

A marker on a line
you cannot see.

Tugu Khatulistiwa marks the area crossed by the equator on Jalan Khatulistiwa in Batu Layang, North Pontianak. It is more than a photo stop: this place connects geography, astronomy and the history of mapping.

At zero degrees latitude, the Earth is read as two hemispheres. In Pontianak, that invisible idea is given a form—a ring, an arrow and a place to pause.

02 · LAYERS OF TIME

From a simple stake
to a city icon.

The first version was installed in 1928 as a geographical-survey marker. Its form evolved in several stages, while the present monument protects traces of the early marker within its complex.

  1. 1928

    An initial stake-and-arrow marker, according to Indonesia.travel.

  2. 1930

    A ring and arrow were added to the marker.

  3. 1938

    Development incorporating four belian timber posts.

  4. 1990–91

    A protective structure and replica developed in 1990–1991, inaugurated September 1991.

Historical summary based on Indonesia.travel and public material from Pontianak City Government.

03 · LOOK UP

When shadows
contract.

Main solar culmination occurs when the Sun is at the zenith; upright objects can cast very short shadows. This seasonal observation is not a daily show or a fixed 12:00 appointment.

Astronomical timing is calculated for a location and year; weather affects visibility rather than the calculated instant. Check current BMKG and city announcements. The city report of 23 March 2026 records that event only.

04 · BEFORE YOU GO

A visit with
more ease.

Use this as a preparation list. Operational information can change; check official channels or speak to on-site staff before travelling.

A

Hours & fee

Maps checked 19 October 2026 lists 08:00–17:00 daily. Indonesia.travel notes a levy introduced in February 2024, without confirming current prices. Ask staff about charges, categories and included services.

B

A comfortable time

Morning or late afternoon is usually more comfortable for walking and photographs. Use sun protection, carry drinking water and plan for tropical rain.

C

Time & etiquette

Allow around 45–90 minutes for the marker, educational area and photographs. Follow site signs, keep the area clean and ask about any special photography rules during events.

FACILITY NOTE

Ask staff about toilets, parking availability, capacity and access routes before relying on them. Facilities and information rooms are not guaranteed to be open.

08 · FAQ

Things worth
knowing.

01Is there an admission fee for the Equator Monument?+

Yes. Pontianak City says a visitor levy has applied since February 2024. Current prices are unverified; ask staff about charges and what is included.

02When is the best time to visit?+

For a regular visit, morning or late afternoon reduces heat exposure. For culmination, check BMKG and city announcements for the location and current year; old events are not a future schedule.

03How long should I allow?+

As a planning suggestion, set aside about 45–90 minutes to see the marker, read the information, take photographs and rest. Add time on weekends or during events.

04Are parking and toilets available?+

Current toilet and parking availability has not been verified. Ask staff about location, condition, capacity and charges before relying on them.

05Is the site wheelchair-friendly?+

We did not find sufficiently detailed, current public information to guarantee step-free access throughout. Contact or ask the manager before visiting if you need specific access support.
